samples.question: The picture shows five horizontal LANES stacked one above another. Each lane holds exactly one solid coloured bar -- one red, one green, one blue, one orange and one purple -- and exactly one solid BLACK upright tick, which is taller than the bar and is that lane's own TARGET. A lane's tick belongs only to that lane: read every bar against the black tick drawn in the same lane and never against any other lane's tick. A bar STOPS SHORT when its right-hand end lies to the LEFT of its own tick, and its SHORTFALL is the horizontal distance from that end rightwards to the tick. Some bars instead run PAST their own tick, so the tick is drawn across them; those bars have no shortfall at all and can never be the answer, however far past the tick they run. The answer is the colour of the bar with the LARGEST SHORTFALL. In every picture at least two bars stop short and at least one bar runs past its tick, and the largest bar-to-tick distance in the picture always belongs to a bar that runs PAST its tick, so unsigned distance is a trap. Where a bar begins, how long it is and how much colour it carries are all uninformative: in every picture the longest bar, the shortest bar, the bar starting furthest left, the bar whose end lies furthest left and the lane whose tick stands furthest right each belong to a colour that is NOT the answer, and the top-to-bottom position of a lane is the answer no more often than chance allows. The pale grey vertical rules, the pale grey lane lines and the grey stubs at the left edge are decoration and mean nothing. Which colour's bar has the largest shortfall? Answer red, green, blue, orange or purple.
